'''Henri Atlan''' (born 27 December 1931) is a French biophysicist and philosopher.

==Early life and education==
Born to a Jewish family in French Algeria, Atlan gained degrees in [[medicine]] and [[biophysics]] at the [[University of Paris]] (now [[University Paris Diderot]]). He married [[Liliane Atlan]] in 1952; they had two children while living in Paris, Miri in 1953 and Michael in 1956.<ref name="JWA">{{cite web|last1=Schneider |first1=Judith Morganroth |title=Liliane Atlan |url=https://jwa.org/encyclopedia/article/Atlan-Liliane |website=Jewish Women's Archive|access-date=30 May 2018}}</ref> He then moved to the [[University of California, Berkeley]] working on ageing<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Atlan|first1=Henri|last2=Miquel|first2=Jaime|last3=Helmle|first3=Leland C.|last4=Dolkas|first4=Constantin B.|year=1976|title=Thermodynamics of aging in Drosophila melanogaster|journal=Mechanisms of Ageing and Development|volume=5
|issue=5|pages=371–387|doi=10.1016/0047-6374(76)90035-X|pmid=823385|s2cid=29989186|issn=0047-6374}}</ref> and mutation.

==Career and thought==
Influenced by [[Heinz von Foerster]], Atlan became interested in applying [[cybernetics]] and [[information theory]] to living organisms, and went to the [[Weizmann Institute]] in [[Rehovot]] to work under the biophysicist [[Aharon Katchalsky]].<ref name="Dupuy" >{{Cite book |last=Dupuy |first=Jean-Pierre |author-link=Jean-Pierre Dupuy |chapter=Henri Atlan (pp. 393—6)|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bREQibN9i-sC&q=%22Henri+Atlan%22&pg=PA393 |editor-last=Kritzman |editor-first=Lawrence D. <!-- https://books.google.com/books?id=bREQibN9i-sC&pg=PR4&dq=%22Edited+by+Lawrence+D.+Kritzman%22%22French+articles+translated+by+Malcolm+DeBevoise%22 --> |editor-link=Lawrence D. Kritzman |others=French articles translated by Malcolm DeBevoise |title=The Columbia History of Twentieth-Century French Thought |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bREQibN9i-sC | year=2007 |orig-date=2006 |publisher=[[Columbia University Press]] |location=New York City |isbn=978-0-2311-0790-7 }}</ref> In 1972, he returned to Paris; and, in that year, his 1972 work on information theory and [[Self-organization in cybernetics|self-organising systems]], entitled ''L'organisation biologique et la théorie de l'information'', received a wide readership.{{citation needed|date=July 2012}} In this book, he proposed the principle of "[[complexity]] from [[Noise (signal processing)|noise]]"<ref>See [https://www.google.com/search?&tbm=bks&q=inauthor:%22Henri+Atlan%22%22complexity+from+noise%22 occurrences] on [[Google Books]].</ref><ref>{{cite book |editor-last=François |editor-first=Charles |editor-link=Charles François (systems scientist) |title=[[International Encyclopedia of Systems and Cybernetics]] |year=2011 |orig-date=1997 |edition=2nd |publisher=[[Walter de Gruyter]] |location=[[Berlin]] |page=[https://books.google.com/books?id=XCn2mn98uEAC&dq=%22complexity+from+noise+principle%22+Atlan+1972&pg=PA107 107] |isbn=978-3-1109-6801-9 }}</ref> ({{langx|fr|le principe de complexité par le bruit}}),<ref>See [https://www.google.com/search?&tbm=bks&q=inauthor:%22Henri+Atlan%22%22complexité+par+le+bruit%22 occurrences] on Google Books.</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.google.com/search?q=%22complexit%C3%A9+par+le+bruit%22%22L%27Organisation+biologique+et+la+th%C3%A9orie+de+l%27information%22+1972|title="complexité par le bruit""L'Organisation biologique et la théorie de l'information" 1972 - Google Search|website=www.google.com}}</ref> concept taken up in his following book ''Entre le cristal et la fumée'' (1979)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.google.com/search?q=%22complexit%C3%A9+par+le+bruit%22%22Entre+le+cristal+et+la+fum%C3%A9e%22+1979|title="complexité par le bruit""Entre le cristal et la fumée" 1979 - Google Search|website=www.google.com}}</ref> and development of 1960 Von Foerster's notion of "order from noise". In Paris, he then taught biophysics at the [[Hôtel-Dieu de Paris|Hôtel-Dieu]] and, later, at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]]'s [[Hadassah Medical Center]].<ref name="Dupuy" /><ref name="EU">{{in lang|fr}} {{Cite encyclopedia |title=Dictionnaire des Idées & Notions en Sciences de la vie et de la Terre. (Les Dictionnaires d'Universalis) |year=2015 |encyclopedia=[[Encyclopædia Universalis]] |isbn=978-2-85229131-7 |last1=Universalis |first1=Encyclopaedia }}</ref>

His participation with [[Francisco Varela]] at a conference in [[Cerisy-la-Salle]] encouraged interest in [[cognitive science]] in France.<ref name="Dupuy" /> Atlan was instrumental in the establishment of the [[Centre de Recherche en Epistémologie Appliquée]] (CREA) at the [[École Polytechnique]], and was appointed in 1983 to the [[Comité Consultatif National d'Ethique|Comité Consultatif National d'Éthique pour la Sciences de a Vie et de la Santé]] (National Advisory Committee on Ethics in the Life Sciences and Medicine). He is director of studies in the philosophy of biology at the ''[[School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences|École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales]]'', and professor emeritus of biophysics at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University|University of Paris VI: Pierre et Marie-Curie]].<ref name="EU"/> He is also a member of [[Collegium International]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.collegium-international.org/en/presentation/members.html |title=Members - Collegium International |access-date=9 August 2019}}</ref> an organization of leaders with political, scientific, and ethical expertise whose goal is to provide new approaches in overcoming the obstacles in the way of a peaceful, socially just, and an economically sustainable world.
